subject: Dynamical systems
hook: DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Dynamical systems don’t require a smooth manifold—any set (even without geometric structure) equipped with a semigroup can serve as the state space

"From a mathematics perspective in the most general case the state space X is treated as a generic set of abstract algebra. This space X has a semi‑group structure on it..." (Wikipedia, Mathematical intuition)
title: Why Dynamical Systems Don't Need Smooth Space
description: Most people assume dynamic systems require calculus, smooth geometry, or physical dimensions. In reality, the mathematical foundation requires neither space nor continuous time to operate. An abstract set and an algebraic operation are sufficient.
narration: DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture swinging clock pendulums, orbiting planets, or continuous trajectories flowing across smooth geometric manifolds. You assume motion demands differential equations and smooth physical space. It does not. Under its broadest mathematical definition, physical space-time completely vanishes. Any arbitrary set, entirely stripped of geometric structure, serves as the state space—advancing step by step solely through an associative algebraic semigroup with a base identity element. Dynamics never needed physical space, just a bare algebraic rule.
